result.title: Approximate Recall, Approximate Forecasts: Recall as a Diagnostic for LLM Forecasting Errors
result.comment: 16 pages, 7 figures (including appendix). Accepted as a Spotlight at the ICML 2026 Workshop on Forecasting as a New Frontier of Intelligence
result.summary: Large Language Models (LLMs) exhibit approximate recall: they retain coarse associations about past events while losing fidelity on specific details. Past research on LLMs has quantified different models' forecasting ability in real-world events using prediction markets, but has not studied how losing said fidelity impacts their forecasting abilities. For example: while an LLM correctly recalls that the answer to: ''Did Anna Sawai win the Best Drama Actress in the 76th Emmy Awards?'' is ''Yes,'' it incorrectly states the event date as September 22 rather than September 15. In this paper, we introduce a novel metric called the Recall Fidelity Score to study how imprecision in internalized knowledge propagates to forecasting capability on future events. On resolved historical markets, we find that higher local recall fidelity around semantically similar past events predicts lower forecasting error on resolved markets, and the same signal predicts smaller distance from open markets prices.

AI.brief_summary: 论文提出「Recall Fidelity Score」度量 LLM 对相近历史事件的内部知识精确度，并在已结算的预测市场上检验这种细节保真度与后续预测误差、与未结算市场价格偏离度的关系。
AI.relevance_reason: 该文把「内部知识保真度」与下游预测误差挂钩的诊断思路，可能启发核查 LVR 中视觉细节是否被忠实保留、其精度损失又如何传导到推理结论与证据筛选。
